title: Illustration - xkcd Stick-Figure Rework
summary: A style-transfer prompt that reworks any reference image (UI mockup, concept diagram, screenshot, photo) into the visual vocabulary of an xkcd webcomic by Randall Munroe — black ink on white, simple stick figures with featureless round heads, hand-lettered ALL-CAPS labels that always stay legible, sparing diagrammatic flourishes (arrows, brackets, dashed inference lines, hash-mark axes, whimsical units like ±5%). Sidesteps the uncanny-face and garbled-text failure modes of more painterly styles, because the xkcd style language *requires* legible hand-lettering and abstracted figures. Works as image-to-image in gpt-image-2 (or any i2i edit model that respects layout, e.g. wan-2.7-image-edit on DeepInfra); pairs naturally with technical explainers, infographics, system diagrams, and any subject where label legibility matters more than ornament.
prompt:
Rework the given image into the style of an xkcd webcomic by Randall Munroe. Convert all subjects to simple stick figures: round, featureless bald heads (just a circle), thin black-ink line bodies with stick limbs, hands drawn as small loops or terminal dots, no facial detail unless absolutely required (and then only the bare minimum — a single eye dot or eyebrow line). Strip all color and retain only solid black ink on a clean white background, with at most the very occasional small flat-color dot or block for emphasis (think xkcd's rare red/blue accent on a single element).

Preserve the layout and spatial relationships of the original — transform the rendering style first, redraw the subjects second, so labels, buildings, devices, and key elements stay where they are. Keep line weight consistent and slightly imperfect — clearly hand-drawn, not vector-perfect.

All text in the image must be HAND-LETTERED ALL-CAPS in clean legible block letters with a slightly uneven baseline (the canonical xkcd handwriting). Lettering must always be readable — do not garble, smudge, or replace with squiggle-text. Re-letter every label, sign, and annotation from the original in this style.

Add small diagrammatic flourishes where they fit the subject: thin arrows pointing from labels to elements, square brackets enclosing groups, dashed lines for hidden / inferred / 'this never happens' connections, hash-mark axis ticks if there are quantities, error-bar whiskers, and whimsical units like '±5%', '(CITATION NEEDED)', or '~' for approximation. Use them sparingly — every flourish should clarify, not decorate.

The overall aesthetic should feel hand-drawn but mathematically precise: sparse, generous whitespace, no clutter, no shading, no gradients, no perspective tricks. A small one-line caption in the same hand-lettered style may sit centered under the panel if the original image had a title or topic worth distilling.

Negative prompt: no color realism, no shading or gradients, no realistic faces, no detailed hair or clothing texture, no anti-aliased soft strokes, no rainbow or pastel palette, no children's-illustration cuteness, no 3D rendering, no photo-realistic elements, no sparkles, no decorative scribbles unrelated to the subject, no garbled or illegible text, no hand-lettering with random non-letter glyphs.
